newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese workers increasingly seen leaving the land.
newsitem.headline: Chinese workers increasingly seen leaving the land.

text.p: Workers in China's agricultural sector will fall over the next five years while those in manufacturing and the service sector will rise, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
Employees in the farm sector would decrease by 2.6 percent a year over the next five years, the newspaper said.

"By 2000 employees in the agricultural sector will account only for 43 percent of the total labour force," the newspaper said. That compared to 52.2 percent in 1990 and 68.7 percent in 1980, it added.
Workers in industry were seen growing by 3.5 percent a year while those in the service sector would rise an annual 7.2 percent, it said.
Industry would employ 25.3 percent of the nation's workers by 2000 while 31.7 percent of the labour force would have jobs in the service sector, it said without giving comparative figures.
The migration each year of millions of farmers to the more prosperous eastern coastal regions was one of the main causes of the change in the country's job structure, China Daily said.
